prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Rebuild this single Cartoon squid/cephalopod sprite for FIRE2.BMP frame006 with corrected face orientation. Image1 is the exact original pixel geometry: head/mantle occupies the LEFT, with arms trailing and curling across the RIGHT in a low wide composition. It is authoritative for the body trajectory, separate arm gaps, shape and proportions. Image2 is a REJECTED earlier drawing: use ONLY its vermilion/red-orange material, golden cel highlights and dark clean Cartoon outline. Do NOT copy its one-eyed face, upward gaze, or reclining orientation.
User correction, mandatory: TWO clearly visible eyes. Put the face at the LOWER-LEFT FRONT of the mantle. Show two distinct white eyes, each with a dark pupil, side by side in a readable three-quarter frontal view. The farther eye can be slightly smaller but must be clearly visible, not hidden. Both pupils look outward LEFT, slightly downward, never up. Do not place a single eyeball on the upper/back surface of the head. The pair of eyes must read as an actual forward-facing face on the left, not two unrelated eye ornaments. Preserve the red mantle and right-trailing curved arms of the first source; do not flip the body, turn it into a fish or redesign the limb arrangement. No mouth is necessary; emphasize the two eye shapes and their intentional leftward gaze.
Warm polished hand-drawn Cartoon rendering matching the earlier palette only, dark warm outlines, red mantle and red-orange arms with yellow highlights inside the contours. One complete isolated creature on true transparent RGBA; preserve transparent spaces between arms. Keep all artwork within a clear safety margin on every side. No human hands, bones, plate, logs, ground, water, scene, external glow, shadow, labels or extra animals. Original small colors are diagnostic, not palette authority. Render the corrected two-eyed left-facing identity, not the rejected one-eyed upward-looking pose.
